newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen firm on pre-holiday short covering.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen firm on pre-holiday short covering.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen futures edged up on Monday as players covered short positions after last week's sell-off.
Dealers said there was little fresh news to inspire trade and participants were mainly adjusting their positions before a Japanese holiday on Tuesday.
"Overall the market is very quiet. Everybody is just sidelined until after the Golden Week holidays," a trader with a Japanese futures house said.

December Euroyen stood at 98.98 at 1110 GMT after hitting a high of 99.00 against its IMM close at 98.96. Volume was low at 10,915 lots. Japanese government bond (JGB) futures for June ended at 125.41 against 125.57 previously.

The Japanese interest rate market came under pressure on Friday as news that Nissan Mutual Life Insurance Co had been ordered to suspend operations caused heavy selling of JGBs on fears the company would move to liquidate its bond holdings.
A trader with a U.S. house said December Euroyen looked well supported around 98.92.
"I would still look to buy around 98.92 but I'd sell around 99.05/06," he said, adding that Japanese interest rates were likely to remain unchanged until at least September.
"Every time the economy looks like it's picking up, they come up with another piece of bad news," he said.
Eurodollar futures finished little changed in very thin trade as participants awaited a slew of U.S. economic data, including quarterly employment data on Tuesday and non-farm payrolls on Friday.
December Eurodollars ended unchanged against their IMM close at 93.375.
